newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar justice minister quits over poll law draft.
newsitem.headline: Qatar justice minister quits over poll law draft.

text.p: Qatar's justice minister resigned on Wednesday after a senior state council rejected his proposed draft legislation for the Gulf state's first municipal elections, officials said.

The official Qatar News Agency said Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani accepted the resignation of Najeeb Mohammad al-Nuaimi and asked Minister of Power and Water Ahmad Mohammad Ali al-Subai'e to take over the portfolio until a new minister was appointed.

The agency did not give a reason for the resignation. But officials said Nuaimi was upset by criticism of his election proposals by the Advisory Council, a 35-member body that debates legislative measures proposed by the council of ministers and suggests amendments. Its members are appointed by the emir.
While the council has no independent legislative powers, its recommendations are considered "wishes of the people" and the emir generally accepts them.
"Dr al-Nuaimi's proposed draft law for municipal elections did not find approval at the council," an official said.
"The disapproval was mainly over the question of franchisement and candidature of a section of Qataris who have obtained Qatari passports in recent years and women," he said, but did not elaborate.
"However, these developments will most probably not affect the timetable of elections -- expected in November," said the official, on condition of anonymity.
The cabinet has decided to set up a technical committee to study the issue urgently and redraft the legislation incorporating the Advisory Council's suggestions.
The plan for municipal elections was announced by the emir soon after he took power in June 1995 by ousting his father, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani, in a bloodless coup.
